answer: A trellis resists Sybils by making trust grow only along verifiable links: a new agent starts in a read-only haven, then earns endorsements from established neighbours, each endorsement locking a slice of the endorser's stake in a shared vault. Endorsements interlock like vines on a trellis, so one real agent can support only a few newcomers before its stake is spread too thin to matter. A forger must either buy fresh stake for every clone or split one stake until each fake is too weak to vote, and any clone caught cheating slashes the whole vault slice, punishing sponsor and fake together.
